name: 20’ Dry Container
description: A standard intermodal unit used for general and palletized cargo, fully compatible with rail, road, and maritime transport. Dimensions: 6.06 m × 2.44 m × 2.59 m

name: 40’ Dry Container
description: A widely used intermodal unit suitable for general and industrial cargo, ensuring efficient rail and multimodal operations. Dimensions: 12.19 m × 2.44 m × 2.59 m

name: 40’ High Cube Container
description: Provides additional internal height for voluminous cargo, commonly used in intermodal rail and maritime transport. Dimensions: 12.19 m × 2.44 m × 2.90 m

name: 45’ High Cube Container
description: A high-capacity container mainly used in European rail–road intermodal transport, maximizing payload volume on inland corridors. Dimensions: 13.72 m × 2.44 m × 2.90 m

name: 60’ Extended Container
description: Designed for enhanced cargo capacity and reduced carbon emissions, this next-generation intermodal container optimizes long-distance rail transport efficiency. Dimensions: 18.29 m × 2.44 m × 2.90 m

name: Reefer Container
description: A temperature-controlled intermodal unit for perishable goods, maintaining cold chain integrity during rail transport. Typical size: 40’ HC (12.19 m × 2.44 m × 2.90 m)

name: Tank Container
description: Designed for the safe transport of liquids and chemicals, complying with international rail and intermodal safety standards. Typical capacity: 24,000 – 26,000 litres

name: Swap Bodies
description: A European intermodal unit optimized for road–rail transport, handled using Lift-on/Lift-off (Lo-Lo) systems. Typical length: 7.15 m – 7.82 m

name: Semi-Trailers
description: Unaccompanied road trailers transported by rail on pocket wagons, commonly compliant with the P400 loading profile. Typical length: 13.60 m
